scope: Proposition 16.1 (One cap step) of the manuscript “Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model” (preprints/Critical-mixing-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3ac6296cc238bae9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 125. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a bounded child field range for the one-off evaluation conclusion below. There are a sufficiently large absolute K0 and a sufficiently small ratio γ > 0 with the following property. Choose σ as a sufficiently high fixed power of γ, and then choose δ as a still higher fixed power, allowing these tolerances to depend on the prescribed field range. Let a parent potential at scale p be intrinsic to the capped data, satisfy the value and gradient comparisons above, and satisfy (16.2) at all fields in (16.1). Use the semiconcave extension just described when forming an auxiliary child potential. For a true parent, retain the true child potential. Condition on the parent data and used auxiliary randomness Fp described below, on which these hypotheses and the Fp-measurable parent-level conclusions of the static comparison hold, including the projected posterior tail and moment bounds for this capped parent. The separate o(1) failure probability used to obtain these parent conclusions remains outside the conditional estimate below. Then, uniformly over such parent data, the probability over the unused Haar refinement O that (16.2) fails at c = γp anywhere on the child annulus is at most Ce−akp + Ce−a′kc for fixed positive a, a′. The same inequalities hold with strict slack on the complementary event. These failure probabilities are summable over the geometric cap list. At intermediate ratios c/p ∈ [γ, 1), if the frozen parameter stays inside the agreement domain with fixed slack, the transverse error and mixed block tend to zero with the parent errors, the total scaled Hessian is bounded, and the radial deficit is at least 0.26. The same deterministic evaluation bounds hold for c/p ∈ [γ2, γ] under this interior-parameter condition. For a true parent and the prescribed bounded child field range there is also a sufficiently small fixed evaluation-ratio interval on which the upper child curvature is at most C/c2, with C depending only on that field range. This last evaluation uses supports centered at the frozen parameter, constructed at the end of the proof. All statements are uniform down to np3 ≍ √ log n.
